The NCIC linkage is the concrete path by which local plate reads can reach federal immigration targeting.

incidents.title: Crime reduction statistics (2025)
incidents.summary: PPD reports 40% reduction in violent crime, 50% reduction in homicides (9 vs 15 through Aug 2024), drive-by shootings down from 118 to 84.
incidents.status: Chief Noeller credits RTCC technology as 'force multiplier'.

incidents.title: Officer shootings by repeat offenders
incidents.summary: March 2025: 3 officers shot by MS-13 gang member with 14 prior felony arrests. April 2025: 2 officers shot in head by repeat offender. Chief Noeller pushing for criminal justice reform.
incidents.status: Chief stated 'blood of my officers is on steps of capitol' regarding soft-on-crime legislation.

incidents.title: IA / POST escalation flow
incidents.summary: Complaints start with Pueblo PD Internal Affairs; criminal issues escalate to DA/POST; systemic issues via AG Pattern & Practice form.
incidents.status: Need standardized evidence packets and tracking.

incidents.title: Flock-ICE Scandal: 1,400+ Immigration Searches via Colorado ALPR Network
incidents.summary: Out-of-state agencies and Border Patrol ran 1,400+ searches with ICE/immigration justifications via Denver's Flock national lookup feature. 690 searches post-Trump inauguration. Loveland PD admitted sharing portal with ICE federal agent. Pueblo's Downtown Association Flock cameras potentially accessible via national network.
incidents.status: ACTION: CORA Pueblo PD to confirm if national lookup enabled; demand City Council resolution prohibiting ICE data sharing.

incidents.title: EFF Exposes Flock Surveillance of Protesters Nationwide
incidents.summary: EFF analyzed 12+ million Flock searches. 50+ agencies ran hundreds of protest-related searches. Tulsa PD: 38 protest searches. Delaware State Police: 9 searches targeting animal-rights activists. Border Patrol accessed during trial period.
incidents.status: ACTION: CORA audit logs for Pueblo ALPR searches by external agencies; demand warrant requirement.

incidents.title: Pueblo Police Racial Disparities in Deadly Force (2013-2023)
incidents.summary: Police Scorecard data shows Black persons 2.8x more likely and Latinx persons 2x more likely to be killed by Pueblo police than white persons. 57% of arrests for low-level, non-violent offenses. More racial disparities than 54% of departments evaluated.
incidents.status: ACTION: Demand demographic impact analysis before surveillance expansions; push for civilian oversight commission.

incidents.title: Colorado ALPR Warrant Legislation Pending
incidents.summary: Sen. Amabile's proposed law would require warrant based on probable cause for police to share ALPR data with other agencies, parallel to GPS/cellphone tracking requirements.
incidents.status: ACTION: Organize community testimony supporting bill; coordinate with ACLU-CO.

incidents.title: HIGHEST-VALUE NEGATIVE: Colorado ALPR warrant bill SB26-070 (PEEPS Act) DIED - no new state law
incidents.summary: Bipartisan bill (Sens. Amabile D-Boulder, Zamora Wilson R-El Paso; Reps. Zokaie, Nguyen) would have required a warrant to query ALPR data more than 72 hours after an offense, imposed a ~30-day retention cap, mandated access logging, required ANNUAL PUBLIC REPORTS listing the number and locations of surveillance devices, restricted out-of-jurisdiction and third-party sharing, made ALPR location data non-public under CORA, given the AG enforcement authority, and created an exclusionary rule. Passed Senate Judiciary 5-2 on 2026-02-23/24; Amabile pulled it from the Senate floor 2026-04-29/30 - 'we didn't have the votes.' Would have taken effect August 2026. Named opposition: Colorado Association of Chiefs of Police, County Sheriffs of Colorado, Colorado District Attorneys' Council, multiple city governments - plus a Polis veto threat over the warrant requirement. Pueblo's chief and sheriff belong to two of those associations.
incidents.status: DEAD. Pueblo PD and PCSO operate under NO state-mandated ALPR retention cap, NO warrant requirement, NO audit-log disclosure duty, and NO public device-inventory obligation. ACTION: drop any messaging assuming a 2026 state law exists; reframe as a local ordinance or administrative directive using the bill text as model language (bipartisan, cleared committee = political cover).

incidents.title: SB26-071 'SAFE Act' postponed indefinitely 6-1 - second Colorado reform bill dead
incidents.summary: The Surveillance Accountability and Freedom Ensured Act (Sen. Lynda Zamora Wilson, R-Colorado Springs) would, from 2027-07-01, have required a warrant for facial recognition (exigent imminent-threat exception only), restricted ALPR and traffic cameras to public spaces and enumerated purposes, set per-technology retention caps with mandatory destruction, banned sale of surveillance data, permitted inter-agency sharing only for active investigations where the recipient also complies, mandated BIENNIAL ATTORNEY GENERAL AUDITS with civil enforcement, required free compliance information to residents, and created a private right of action. Introduced 2026-01-28, laid over unamended 2026-02-23, postponed indefinitely by Senate Judiciary 2026-05-06 on a 6-1 vote. The Colorado Municipal League opposed it.
incidents.status: DEAD. The AG-audit and biennial-reporting provisions were the strongest oversight architecture proposed in Colorado. ACTION: lift the SAFE Act retention/destruction schedule and audit language verbatim into a proposed Pueblo ordinance - it is a Republican-sponsored bill, which defuses the 'partisan overreach' objection with a GOP-majority council.

incidents.title: HB26-1037 (ban on government purchase of personal data from brokers) killed
incidents.summary: Would have barred law enforcement and government entities from purchasing or otherwise obtaining for value personal data from third-party brokers, and barred agencies from sharing personal data among themselves, with carve-outs only for a judicial warrant, subpoena, court order, individual consent, or emergency. Postponed indefinitely by House Judiciary 2026-04-22.
incidents.status: DEAD. Data-broker purchases remain a legal, unlogged bypass around every warrant requirement, and Flock's Nova product is built on aggregated public-records and commercial data. ACTION: add 'any contract, subscription, or trial with a data broker or people-search product, including Flock Nova, Thomson Reuters CLEAR, LexisNexis Accurint, TransUnion TLOxp, or Peregrine' to the standing CORA template.

incidents.title: COMPLIANCE HOOK: HB26-1276 SIGNED - penalties for sharing personal info with federal immigration agencies
incidents.summary: The one surveillance-adjacent Colorado statute that PASSED in 2026. Sponsors Reps. Velasco and Garcia, Sens. Jodeh and Weissman. Passed House 42-21, Senate 23-12; signed by Gov. Polis 2026-06-04. Increases penalties for local authorities who share personal information with federal immigration agencies; expands CDPHE authority to inspect immigration detention facilities with civil penalties for non-compliance; creates an immigration facility inspection fund ($107,283 appropriated); requires the POST Board to establish training standards on peace officer compliance with laws concerning civil immigration detainers, with officers to complete training BY 2027-12-31; directs the Attorney General to develop and publish a policy on protection of personal identifying information. It does NOT mention ALPR or license plate reader data. Amended at the governor's request to strip a provision barring state agencies from complying with immigration enforcement subpoenas.
incidents.status: IN EFFECT. Strongest live compliance hook of this refresh, but it governs personal information sharing, not sensors - the fight is whether a plate read counts as PII. ACTION: (1) once the AG publishes the required PII-protection policy, CORA both Pueblo agencies for their conforming policy and ask IN WRITING whether they treat ALPR reads and RTCC video as PII under it; (2) track the POST immigration-detainer training standard and CORA completion rosters against the 2027-12-31 deadline; (3) the detention-facility inspection authority applies to the Walsenburg/CoreCivic and Hudson/GEO facilities already in the repo.

incidents.title: HB26-1312 SIGNED - Colorado POST Board restructured, civilian seats reduced
incidents.summary: Sponsors Rep. Chad Clifford, Sen. Kyle Mullica. Introduced 2026-03-02, House 2026-04-21, Senate 2026-05-01, signed 2026-06-03, effective 2026-08-12. Reduces law-enforcement leadership seats AND reduces non-law-enforcement (civilian) members while increasing line-officer representation; adds training-academy and reserve-officer representatives; sets minimum certification age at 21; bars POST from approving skills instructors or academies holding revoked certifications as of 2026-09-01; requires the AG to propose academy training updates by 2030-12-31.
incidents.status: IN EFFECT 2026-08-12. Net effect is FEWER civilian members and MORE line officers on the state body that decertifies officers - a reduction in civilian oversight capacity at the exact venue the repo's complaint-escalation workflow routes to. ACTION: update IA/DA/POST/AG escalation guidance to set realistic expectations about POST; shift weight to the AG Pattern & Practice route and civil litigation.

incidents.title: SB26-152 SIGNED - bans per-citation vendor pay for automated enforcement
incidents.summary: Sponsors Sens. Matt Ball and Byron Pelton, Reps. Jenny Willford and Carlos Barron. Introduced 2026-03-31, signed 2026-06-02, effective 2026-08-12. Key procurement provision: vendor compensation must be a flat monthly fee or flat hourly rate and may NOT include incentives, bonuses, or escalators related to the number of citations issued. Also establishes registered-owner liability with sale/lease/stolen defenses; under variable or temporary speed reductions, citations only for exceeding the regular posted maximum; restructures penalty amounts; civil penalties rise starting 2035-01-01.
incidents.status: IN EFFECT 2026-08-12. A narrow but genuine win and a usable audit standard. ACTION: when any Pueblo automated-enforcement contract surfaces, CORA the compensation schedule and check it against the flat-fee mandate - a per-citation term after 2026-08-12 is a straightforward violation.

incidents.title: HB26-1071 (Pueblo's bid for municipal interstate speed cameras) died; Pueblo Council backed it
incidents.summary: Prime sponsor Rep. Tisha Mauro (Pueblo). Would have let cities and counties place automated vehicle identification systems on federal interstates, currently a state-only power. Introduced 2026-01-27; House committee 8-3 on 2026-02-17; House 3rd reading passed 37-22 on 2026-02-23; Senate committee 5-2 on 2026-03-19; Senate 2nd reading passed 2026-04-20; Senate 3rd reading laid over to 2026-05-14, one day after the General Assembly adjourned 2026-05-13. LOST. Pueblo City Council formally resolved in support at its 2026-02-09 meeting.
incidents.status: DEAD. Documents that Pueblo's council and its state representative were actively seeking MORE automated enforcement authority in the same session they declined to act on ALPR limits. ACTION: cite the 2026-02-09 resolution when council members claim caution about surveillance; watch for the bill's return in 2027.

incidents.title: EFF: ICE-populated NCIC 'Immigration Violator' hotlist can be enabled inside Flock
incidents.summary: Agencies using Flock can subscribe cameras to NCIC topics from a dropdown in the admin interface, including an 'Immigration Violator' file populated EXCLUSIVELY by ICE. Per the NCIC operator manual that file includes people with administrative warrants issued by ICE WITHOUT judicial review, plus vehicle data where ICE has reasonable grounds to believe the subject may be operating a particular vehicle. Every passing plate is compared against it in real time. EFF records requests confirmed it enabled at Blue Island PD (IL) and Sparks PD (NV); 11 other responding agencies had it disabled. NO Colorado agency is named - nobody has asked.
incidents.status: TOP PRIORITY ACTION. Materially worse than the 2025 Denver scandal: that was retrospective searching, this is an automated real-time ICE targeting pipeline. Pueblo PD runs Flock AND runs Genetec Cloudrunner explicitly against NCIC, so the mechanism is present on two systems. ACTION: file the records request using EFF's published template language asking for 'NCIC topics that the agency has selected,' to both Pueblo PD and PCSO; check EyesonFlock.com and AtlasofSurveillance.org first; brief CORRN, El Movimiento Sigue and CIRC; time the request to land with the incoming sheriff.

incidents.title: ATF searched Loveland's Flock data for ICE - disabling 'national lookup' is not sufficient
incidents.summary: An ATF agent searched Loveland CO's Flock data six times in April 2026, and ATF confirmed the searches were conducted in collaboration with ICE. No AG investigation has been announced. Separately, the Colorado Sun confirmed that although Denver pulled its data from Flock's national directory in April 2025, it STILL shares with other Colorado departments whose data other agencies can reach - and a federal agent using Loveland PD's account made 26 ICE-related searches April 3-25, i.e. AFTER Denver's opt-out.
incidents.status: CRITICAL TECHNICAL POINT. In-state sharing plus a single cooperating in-state agency re-opens the federal pathway. ACTION: the CORA ask must be the FULL LIST of agencies Pueblo shares with and receives from, not a yes/no on national lookup; demand removal of all 287(g)-holding agencies per Durango's June 2026 precedent; demand weekly or monthly audits with public reporting per Durango and Thornton.

incidents.title: Colorado precedent: five full Flock cancellations, seven sharing restrictions, four live reviews - Pueblo took no action
incidents.summary: FULL CANCELLATIONS: Denver - administrative non-renewal by Mayor Johnston announced 2026-02-24, contract expired 2026-03-31, all 110 cameras decommissioned and physically removed (largest US removal by camera count), driven by audit logs showing 1,400+ immigration-purpose searches; council then approved an Axon replacement 7-6 on 2026-03-31. Fort Collins - COUNCIL VOTE 6-1 on 2026-06-16, immediate cancellation, data collection halted, all 15 cameras ordered removed, plus a MORATORIUM on new surveillance tech until a policy is written (strongest council-vote precedent, comparable Front Range city). Canon City - MOST TRANSFERABLE TO PUEBLO: small southern Colorado city ~40 miles away, 6 cameras, mechanism was simply LETTING THE CONTRACT EXPIRE (2026-06-08 special meeting, lapsed 2026-06-30); Police Chief John Schick reversed his own prior support citing 'operational concerns, and, frankly, some professional blind spots, particularly concerning data security and external data controls.' Longmont - unanimous non-renewal 2026-03-24 with local data-control requirements, mandatory public reporting and a one-year review attached to the Axon replacement. Aspen - police-chief administrative decision, paused 2026-04-27, discontinued ~2026-07-24; two readers never activated, zero data ever collected. SHARING RESTRICTIONS: Thornton - police department alone, no council vote, contract untouched, REVOKED Flock network access for over 2,100 outside agencies (Feb 2026) with weekly audits. Durango - unanimous council resolution 2026-04-21 requiring monthly public reports; first report 2026-06-17 disclosed ALL agencies holding 287(g) agreements were removed from sharing and DPD audits and denies access weekly; a citizen 'Protect Our Privacy Ordinance' (72-hour retention, judicial warrant, civilian oversight committee) from DeFlock Durango with ACLU-CO and CIRC is still pending. Glenwood Springs - staged administrative shutoff, all outside-agency access blocked 2026-02-11 'regardless of location' after Aspen Journalism found 78 outside agencies including US Border Patrol had run immigration searches; 21 cameras now run only as an internal CCIC/NCIC hotlist network. Boulder - CITY MANAGER administrative rebid announced 2026-03-13 (explicitly not a council matter), Flock extended on renegotiated terms with a 30-day no-penalty opt-out and monthly data-review meetings, RFP for 49 ALPRs still under review as of 2026-07-20; class action filed 2026-05-27 over the 31-camera network under the Colorado Constitution. Snowmass Village - suspended all outside sharing (Mar 2026) after finding 21 agencies including ICE ERO, HSI and US Marshals in its logs. Pitkin County - halted HSI sharing. Carbondale - declined to adopt at all. LIVE REVIEWS: Castle Rock (council directed a vendor comparison 2026-07-21; 32 Flock ALPRs at a 365-DAY retention), Avon (public input 2026-07-28 ahead of renewal, contract terminable on 30 days notice), Silt, Telluride.
sources: Aspen Times, 2026-07-24 and Aspen Public Radio, 2026-07-27
Boulder Reporting Lab, 2026-03-13 and Axios Boulder, 2026-07-20
incidents.status: NO Pueblo city or county action on Flock or ALPR was found anywhere in this window - no council item, no ordinance, no administrative restriction - while Pueblo simultaneously expanded Flock and stood up 70 Cloudrunner cameras. ACTION: (1) lead with Canon City for local credibility and Fort Collins for the council-vote template; (2) because Boulder, Thornton, Glenwood Springs, Aspen, Snowmass and Pitkin all acted WITHOUT a council vote, the chief and city manager can unilaterally disable outside-agency and 287(g) access - make that the first, cheapest ask; (3) FRAME THE ASK AS DATA OWNERSHIP, RETENTION LIMITS AND NO FEDERAL ACCESS, NOT 'drop Flock' - Denver, Longmont, Douglas County, Glenwood Springs and Colorado Springs all migrated to Axon, which holds existing DHS and ICE contracts, and ACLU-CO opposed Denver's Axon replacement. A vendor swap is not a win.

incidents.title: Colorado counter-trend: nearby jurisdictions expanded ALPR and drones in the same window
incidents.summary: Colorado Springs announced ~2026-02-09/10 it would nearly TRIPLE its ALPRs while switching Flock to Axon - attributable to Police Chief Adrian Vasquez administratively, with no council vote found; Mayor Yemi Mobolade published a public defense 2026-04-23. Commerce City council voted 7-2 on 2026-04-06 (Ordinance 2755, with 2756 recognizing $608,900 for 2026) for a 5-year ~$4.56M Flock contract covering ALPRs, drones, cameras, gunshot detection and RTCC tooling. Douglas County approved a $22.8M Axon package 2026-07-14 replacing 50 Flock cameras with 100 Axon Outpost ALPRs plus a countywide drone-first-responder network, with a 30-day purge unless tied to an open case, quarterly sheriff audits and DA oversight - the stated drivers were that the county did not own its own camera data and that a county trailhead camera was HACKED and livestreaming to the open internet. Castle Rock signed a ~$600K 3-year Flock drone contract in June 2026 then opened a review in July. Glenwood Springs approved a $2.4M 10-year Axon contract 7-0. Statewide (Colorado Sun 2026-04-27): ~100 Colorado agencies have Flock partnerships, 160+ private entities involved, 60 agencies statewide use ALPR with 42 holding Flock contracts - Pueblo is inside that 60 but is not named.
incidents.status: Do NOT overstate the retrenchment narrative - cite both columns. The strongest transferable SAFEGUARDS come from the expansion side: Douglas County's data-ownership requirement, 30-day purge, quarterly audits and DA oversight, plus Longmont's local data control and mandatory public reporting, are the concrete terms to demand of Pueblo regardless of vendor. The Douglas County trailhead camera hack is a local-adjacent argument that these systems are a SECURITY liability, not only a privacy one.

incidents.title: Flock 2026 accountability record: audits, breaches, litigation, and one abandoned product
incidents.summary: DAYTON OH (disclosed 2026-06-26): suspended Flock in early May 2026 after finding 7,100+ immigration-related searches of its data (Jul 2023-2026) - 3,703 by Border Patrol, 779 by Lowndes County GA, 1,778 containing 'ICE,' 443 for 'immigration,' 140 outside agencies; July 2025 alone had 6,104 immigration searches vs ~1,000 the prior year and 22 in 2023; the city COULD NOT DETERMINE whether data was returned or acted on. SFPD AUDIT (disclosed 2026-06-18): a routine May 2026 audit found regional fusion center NCRIC had queried SF's Flock network for federal and out-of-state agencies - 299 improper inquiries in about a year, including night-hours access granted to another network's watch center WITHOUT SFPD's knowledge; SFPD cut off NCRIC. This is the fusion-center risk the repo has been asking about, confirmed in practice. LAPD IG AUDIT (2026-07-13): for Aug-Sep 2025, officers acknowledged 161 alerts as accurate plate matches on vehicles that were NOT actually stolen, out of 5,911 plates tracked and 210.5M plate reads; no action taken on 4,575 hot-listed vehicles; LAPD let its Flock contract EXPIRE and suspended new ALPR deployments pending full audit and public input. PERSON-TRACKING (404 Media 2026-07-16): a 'FreeForm' search is used for hundreds of person-descriptor searches ('heavy-set male with a black and white hat,' 'person on skateboard'), some with racial descriptors and political-affiliation indicators, across hundreds of cameras in multiple states. TWO SECURITY INCIDENTS: 2026-01-08 Flock Condor cameras (360-degree PTZ with AI object tracking) were reachable on the open internet with NO username, password or encryption - live video, ~one month of archived footage, and the ability to DELETE video; 60+ exposed camera admin systems findable via ordinary search engines; Flock called it 'a limited, isolated configuration issue.' 2026-06-11 Flock leaked police search reasons, and some searched plates, into DuckDuckGo and Bing indexes. Officers have repeatedly been arrested for using Flock to stalk people (2026-06-10). LITIGATION: Javorsky v. Flock class action filed 2026-02-26 in San Francisco Superior Court (amended 2026-04-03) under California's ALPR Privacy Act, alleging federal agencies accessed SFPD camera data 1.6M+ times in seven months and Los Altos data was shared out-of-state 1M+ times, with audit search reasons literally reading 'CBP,' 'ICE,' 'fresno dea intel'; statutory damages $2,500/violation. ONE ADVOCACY WIN: EFF 2026-07-17, Flock ENDED the rollout of 'Distress Detection,' a citywide microphone feature marketed to detect human screaming; gunshot detection remains and also flags 'community disruption.' Flock also discontinued live video on ALPRs for law enforcement in March 2026 after a 5-agency pilot, and its CEO then claimed the cameras only take 'a static picture of a car,' contradicting Flock's own prior marketing. NOVA SHIPPED, NOT KILLED: a live marketed product federating RMS, CAD, LPR, jail records, public records and 'approved open sources,' advertising 'type in a name, phone number, address, or vehicle'; San Diego PD signed a one-year pilot 2026-04-29 but has not activated it; BERKELEY DECLINED the Nova package 2026-05-08; Flock removed hacked-breach data sources but kept the product. MISSION CREEP (EFF May 2026): ALPR used for school residency verification, background checks and noise complaints. Krishnamoorthi and Robert Garcia) and the 2025-11-03 Wyden/Krishnamoorthi letter urging an FTC Section 5 investigation - the latter noting ~75% of Flock law-enforcement customers opted into the National Lookup Tool per Flock's own disclosure to Congress, and at least 35 Flock customer accounts stolen via infostealer malware. incidents.title: Pueblo County Sheriff reported ZERO months of state-mandated use-of-force data
incidents.summary: Colorado DCJ Office of Research and Statistics, 'Contacts and Use of Force in Colorado: CY2024 Report' (September 2025, pursuant to 24-31-903 C.R.S.). Table 57: Pueblo PD reported 10 of 12 months - 9,244 contacts, 12,695 citizens, 31 use-of-force contacts, force rate 244.2 per 10,000. PUEBLO COUNTY SHERIFF'S OFFICE REPORTED 0 OF 12 MONTHS - zero contacts, zero citizens, zero force - one of 65 of 255 mandated Colorado agencies submitting nothing. Table 58 lists Pueblo PD for 3 law-enforcement-involved civilian deaths in CY2024 (deaths 4/17, 6/19, 7/30/2024; all gunshot; two decedents recorded Hispanic, one White - names in the state report are omitted here). Statewide: force used on Black non-Hispanic individuals at 3,142 per 100,000 contacts vs 531.8 for White NH (~5.9x); Black NH people 3x more likely to be person-searched (7.5% vs 2.4%) yet searches of Black NH and Native American NH people found contraband LESS often (15%, 11%) than White NH (17%) - an inverted hit-rate finding. Statewide IA outcomes: 169 misconduct complaints with 2 sustained (1.2%); 565 post-use-of-force investigations with 21 sustained (3.7%); only ONE agency in the entire state (Aurora PD) reported officer resignations during administrative investigation - Pueblo agencies did not. CRITICAL LIMITATION: agency-level race breakdowns do NOT exist in the published report - Tables 57/58 give Pueblo only aggregate counts and every race/ethnicity table is statewide, so a Pueblo-specific stop or search disparity CANNOT be computed from public data. There is no 2026 release; the CY2025 report is expected ~September 2026.
sources: Colorado DCJ ORS, CY2024 Contacts and Use of Force Report (https://cdpsdocs.state.co.us/ors/Docs/Reports/2025_LEI-Rpt-CY2024.pdf)
Colorado DCJ dashboards (403 to automated fetch)

incidents.title: 10th Circuit clears the way for jury trial against Pueblo County Sheriff defendants

The case - arising from a 2022-02-22 fatal deputy shooting in the Liberty Point International School parking lot in Pueblo West, plus the unlawful seizure and search of the decedent's mother - now proceeds to JURY TRIAL on excessive force and unlawful seizure. incidents.title: Facial recognition: no Pueblo use found, but SB22-113 is the live compliance hook
incidents.summary: NO evidence was found that Pueblo PD or PCSO uses facial recognition, Clearview AI, or any facial recognition service - a genuine negative finding, and the most important one to keep monitoring, because Pueblo already has the camera fabric that FRS bolts onto. Colorado SB22-113 remains in effect and requires any agency, BEFORE using facial recognition, to: file a NOTICE OF INTENT with its reporting authority; publish an ACCOUNTABILITY REPORT of policies and procedures; obtain a WARRANT for ongoing surveillance or real-time/near-real-time identification (narrow exceptions for investigative leads with probable cause, missing persons, decedent ID); conduct operational testing before deployment; and train personnel periodically. It bars FRS results as the SOLE basis for probable cause, requires meaningful human review of legally significant decisions, and prohibits targeting by protected characteristic or First Amendment activity. The task force repeals 2027-09-01 but the substantive restrictions persist. Aurora is the in-state precedent: council authorized APD facial recognition 2025-10-23, and Aurora's public reports page shows exactly what Pueblo would have to publish. Colorado DMV facial recognition is available to police, and use by a Pueblo agency would itself trigger the SB22-113 duties. Separately SB25-143 (effective 2025-07-01) conditionally lifted the school FRS moratorium, permitting districts to use facial recognition to alert staff to individuals who made violent threats, locate missing children on grounds, and alert staff when court-barred individuals enter; systems may remain operational at all times for authorized purposes, biometric data must be deleted within 18 months, and use REQUIRES LOCAL SCHOOL BOARD APPROVAL.
sources: Security Industry Association analysis of SB25-143, 2025-04-08
Aurora facial recognition public reports page
incidents.status: A SB22-113 notice of intent is a PUBLIC RECORD filed with a reporting authority - asking whether one exists is a cheap, high-signal early-warning check. ACTION: (1) ask the City of Pueblo and Pueblo County in writing whether ANY notice of intent or accountability report has been filed, and whether either agency has submitted Colorado DMV facial-recognition requests; (2) because SB25-143 requires LOCAL SCHOOL BOARD APPROVAL, monitoring D60 and D70 board agendas is a free early-warning system for school FRS; (3) set a standing quarterly re-check - this is the vector most likely to change first.

(6) An FOP labor dispute or litigation against PCSO - referenced by the incoming sheriff at a forum, not independently sourced. (7) A Colorado AG investigation into ALPR/ICE data sharing DOES NOT EXIST and an earlier lead was misdated: the AG's Mesa County investigation was announced 2025-06-23, NOT 2026, and concerned a deputy sharing a driver's plate and vehicle description in a SIGNAL GROUP CHAT with DHS officials, not ALPR databases; it was expanded to four agencies in July 2025, the lawsuit against the deputy was later DROPPED, and Mesa County's countersuit was dismissed. DO NOT CITE stateofsurveillance.org, citizenportal.ai, placa.ai, techtimes.com, uticaphoenix.net, newschunks.com. civil_liberties_concerns.issue: Local plate reads flow to an ICE-populated federal hotlist via NCIC
civil_liberties_concerns.details: Pueblo PD's 70 Genetec Cloudrunner ALPR cameras are queried against NCIC, and Flock systems can subscribe to an NCIC 'Immigration Violator' file populated exclusively by ICE - which per the NCIC operator manual includes people with administrative warrants issued by ICE without judicial review. Every passing plate is compared in real time. No Colorado agency has been asked whether this hotlist is enabled.

civil_liberties_concerns.issue: No Colorado ALPR statute exists - every safeguard must be built locally
civil_liberties_concerns.details: SB26-070 (warrant + 30-day retention + public device inventory) died on the Senate floor 2026-04-29; SB26-071 SAFE Act (facial recognition warrant + biennial AG audits) was postponed indefinitely 2026-05-06; HB26-1037 (data-broker purchase ban) died 2026-04-22. Pueblo PD and PCSO therefore operate under no state-mandated retention cap, no warrant requirement, no audit-log disclosure duty and no public device-inventory obligation. Opposition included the Colorado Association of Chiefs of Police and County Sheriffs of Colorado, to which Pueblo's chief and sheriff belong.

civil_liberties_concerns.issue: Drone launch is automated by gunshot detection, gated only by an operator feasibility check
civil_liberties_concerns.details: ShotSpotter gunfire detection automatically triggers BRINC drone deployment in Pueblo. The only stated limit is an operator check for weather, competing missions and coverage - not a warrant or policy review. With 83% of ShotSpotter alerts generating no citizen 911 call, an acoustic false positive can put a thermal-camera drone over a Pueblo address with no human deciding it was worth doing. PPD's public UAV page still describes a 2018 three-drone crime-scene unit.

civil_liberties_concerns.issue: Community Connect Pillars Two through Four are camera federation, not a registry, with no published terms
civil_liberties_concerns.details: Pillars Two (Genetec Cloud Video SaaS), Three (existing Genetec on-premise) and Four (non-Genetec IP) are technical federation of private cameras into a police video management system - materially different from the registry the program is named for. The city publishes no terms of use, no privacy policy, no retention terms, no audit commitment, and no statement of whether the RTCC obtains live streaming access or only request-based pull.

civil_liberties_concerns.issue: Every verbal Pueblo PD safeguard has failed an audit somewhere else in 2026
civil_liberties_concerns.details: Documented query reasons, verified hits, no federal access, no person tracking, no live video - each was audited and found wanting elsewhere in 2026: Dayton found 7,100+ immigration searches and could not determine whether data was acted on; SFPD found 299 improper fusion-center inquiries including undisclosed night-hours access; the LAPD Inspector General found 161 alerts acknowledged as accurate matches on vehicles that were not actually stolen; 404 Media documented hundreds of person-descriptor searches including racial and political-affiliation indicators. Pueblo has published no written ALPR policy, no retention period and no audit logs at all.

civil_liberties_concerns.issue: Surveillance systems are a security liability, not only a privacy one

In June 2026 Flock leaked police search reasons and some searched plates into DuckDuckGo and Bing. A Douglas County trailhead camera was hacked and livestreaming publicly. At least 35 Flock customer accounts have been stolen via infostealer malware. Officers have repeatedly been arrested for using Flock to stalk people.

CORA the Cloudrunner contract, total cost, term length, retention period, written ALPR policy, audit logs and query-justification records - none are public for 70 cameras.
CORA the 70-camera placement map so organizers can route around coverage and the map layer can be updated.
Publicly note that Pueblo now runs TWO parallel ALPR vendors while peer Colorado cities cancelled one.

Reconcile the installed park camera list against the December 2024 $1M authorizing resolution - El Central Park now appears while Ray Aguilera Park and Lake Minnequa have dropped off, with no visible re-authorization.
Resolve the 4-vs-6 mobile camera trailer discrepancy before publishing.

recommendations.theme: Local ordinance strategy after both state bills died (2026-07-29)
actions: Drop all messaging that assumes a 2026 Colorado surveillance law exists - SB26-070, SB26-071 and HB26-1037 all died.

Use SB26-070's own text as model ordinance language: warrant for queries older than 72 hours, ~30-day retention cap, access logging, annual public report listing the number and locations of surveillance devices, sharing restrictions, exclusionary rule. It was bipartisan and cleared committee.
Lift SB26-071's retention/destruction schedule and biennial audit language too - it was Republican-sponsored, which defuses the 'partisan overreach' objection with a GOP-majority council.

Lead with Canon City for local credibility (small southern Colorado city ~40 miles away that simply let its contract expire; its own police chief cited 'professional blind spots… concerning data security and external data controls') and Fort Collins for the council-vote template (6-1, immediate cancellation plus a moratorium on new surveillance tech).

Make the FIRST and cheapest ask administrative, not legislative: Boulder, Thornton, Glenwood Springs, Aspen, Snowmass and Pitkin County all restricted sharing WITHOUT a council vote, so the chief and city manager can act unilaterally.

FRAME THE ASK AS DATA OWNERSHIP, RETENTION LIMITS AND NO FEDERAL ACCESS - NOT 'drop Flock.' Denver, Longmont, Douglas County, Glenwood Springs and Colorado Springs all migrated to Axon, which holds existing DHS and ICE contracts; ACLU-CO opposed Denver's Axon replacement. A vendor swap is not a win.

Borrow safeguards from the expansion side: Douglas County's data-ownership requirement, 30-day purge, quarterly sheriff audits and DA oversight; Longmont's local data control and mandatory public reporting.
Once the Attorney General publishes the personal-identifying-information protection policy required by HB26-1276, CORA both Pueblo agencies for their conforming policy.
Ask both agencies IN WRITING whether they treat ALPR reads and RTCC video as personal identifying information under that policy - the statute does not mention ALPR, so this is the contested ground.
Track the POST Board's immigration-detainer training standard and CORA Pueblo PD/PCSO completion rosters against the 2027-12-31 officer deadline.
Route the expanded CDPHE detention-facility inspection authority to the immigration/ICE agent - it applies to the Walsenburg/CoreCivic and Hudson/GEO facilities already in the repo.

When any Pueblo automated-enforcement contract surfaces, check the vendor compensation schedule against SB26-152's flat-fee mandate (effective 2026-08-12) - a per-citation term is a straightforward violation.

recommendations.theme: Incoming sheriff transition ask (window closes January 2027)
actions: Prepare a short written transition ask for Sheriff-elect Allen Medina now - he campaigned on transparency, ran unopposed in November, and has taken NO public position on surveillance technology.

Ask for: a published ALPR policy with a retention cap; federal and out-of-state sharing disabled; any ICE-populated NCIC hotlist disabled; a commitment to full 24-31-903 C.R.S. contact and use-of-force reporting for CY2025; and published annual audit summaries.
Ask PCSO in writing why ZERO of 12 months of CY2024 use-of-force data were submitted, timed ahead of the ~September 2026 CY2025 state report.
Request a transition meeting before January while commitments are still cheap for him to make.

Records request to Colorado DCJ Office of Research and Statistics for RECORD-LEVEL Pueblo contact/search/force data - the published CY2024 report has no agency-level race breakdowns, so no Pueblo disparity figure can be computed without it.
CORA Pueblo PD Internal Affairs complaint counts, dispositions and median resolution times for 2024-2026 - none are published.
CORA the CIRT reports and body-camera footage for the three officer-involved shootings of 2026-05-14, 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-08.

CORA RTCC logs, ALPR queries and drone flight records for each OIS incident window - the practice of placing dispatchers on leave implies RTCC telemetry is part of the incident record, and this is the cleanest way to test whether the sensor stack drove the response.

POST records request for the certification revocation of the former PPD officer convicted 2026-05-12 of a Class 3 felony - probably the first 2026 Pueblo decertification, but POST publishes no browsable list.
Track the 10th Circuit-cleared PCSO jury trial docket and attend; note that criminal charges were declined while civil liability survived three rounds of qualified-immunity review.

Build the civilian oversight board ask using Colorado Springs and Aurora as precedent; cite the drop in Cases-of-Interest postings (one 2026 entry vs four in 2025) as a measurable transparency regression.
CORA the DFR policy, FAA waivers/COAs and BVLOS authorizations, launch-site list, flight logs, drone-video retention period, and the ShotSpotter-to-drone auto-trigger configuration.

Put PPD's public UAV Unit page (2018 unit, three UAVs, crime-scene documentation) side by side with the vendor case study (BRINC fleet, gunshot-triggered auto-launch, thermal, sirens, two-way audio) in council testimony and the next La Cucaracha editorial - the disclosure gap IS the story.
Demand the UAV page be updated as a condition of any further drone funding.
CORA ShotSpotter alert-level dispositions so the false-positive rate can be computed rather than inferred from the 17% 911-correlation figure.
Archive the SoundThinking Pueblo success-story PDF dated 2026-01-27 - the vendor appears to have pulled it from its site.
CORA the current ShotSpotter contract term and renewal date - Pueblo's absence from SoundThinking's Q2 2026 multi-year renewals announcement is unexplained.

recommendations.theme: New and emerging vectors to monitor (2026-07-29)
actions: Facial recognition: ask the City of Pueblo and Pueblo County in writing whether any SB22-113 notice of intent or accountability report has been filed, and whether either agency has submitted Colorado DMV facial-recognition requests. Aurora's public reports page is the template for what Pueblo would have to publish. Set a standing quarterly re-check - this is the vector most likely to change first.

Schools: because SB25-143 requires LOCAL SCHOOL BOARD APPROVAL for school facial recognition, monitor D60 and D70 board agendas and minutes as a free early-warning system. Also request the CURRENT D60 SRO MOU - the copy on file at the city is dated 2022-01-01 and no data-sharing or student-record-access provision is known.
Obtain and manually read the Motorola Solutions Pueblo County schools case study (image PDF) - Motorola owns Avigilon and Pelco, so this likely documents the D70 camera and analytics stack.
Transit: request TripSpark/MyRide (RidePueblo) data-retention terms and any law-enforcement access provision, plus Pueblo Transit's onboard camera policy - no privacy policy is published at all.

New jail: records request the electronic security stack for the 672-bed facility - cameras, biometrics, body scanners, inmate communications monitoring. Nothing has been disclosed for a $150M build. A new federal counter-drone rule authorizing local police AND corrections agencies to detect and disable drones makes C-UAS a plausible near-term acquisition.

CDOT: request the I-25 Pueblo speed-camera vendor, full retention and access policy, and any law-enforcement or federal sharing provision; submit public comment opposing post-construction retention of the cameras, since CDOT's keep-or-remove decision is live now. Note the 3-year image retention as the benchmark to hold every other Pueblo system against.

Ask specifically whether Pueblo has any Flock Nova pilot, trial or quote - Berkeley's May 2026 refusal is the precedent. Add data brokers and people-search products by name to the standing CORA template, since HB26-1037's purchase ban died.
Demand Pueblo enable Flock's own FREE 'Audit Assistance' tool (launched 2026-04-14) and publish the output - refusing a free first-party audit tool is itself a story.

Re-run searches on the four least-exhausted vectors: cell-site simulators, Colorado Information Analysis Center participation by Pueblo agencies, Pueblo Mall private security integration, and CBI/Colorado State Patrol ALPR.

REMOVE the Palantir framing from all public-facing materials. The Flock-Palantir integration and Thiel-owns-both claims were fact-checked as false by the Colorado Sun on 2026-02-13; Flock's trust page states 'Flock does not work with Palantir.' The ASCII data-flow diagram in opsec/Pueblo 81008 Surveillance.md section 5 and the 'Flock provides the eyes, Palantir provides the brain' quote are a credibility liability - flagged for the owner of opsec/ to revise.
Replace it with the DOCUMENTED pipeline: local plate reads -> CCIC/NCIC -> ICE-populated Immigration Violator hotlist, plus local agencies running searches for federal partners.

Do NOT cite stateofsurveillance.org, citizenportal.ai, placa.ai, techtimes.com, uticaphoenix.net or newschunks.com - AI-generated aggregators. Avoid aggregate cancellation counts ('53 cities') entirely; EFF confirms the trend but publishes no number.
Do not overstate the retrenchment narrative - Colorado Springs is nearly tripling its readers and Commerce City voted 7-2 for a $4.56M expansion in the same window. Cite both columns.

Lead the cost argument with a GOP-majority council: $210K/yr ShotSpotter + ~$200K/yr Genetec licensing + undisclosed Cloudrunner and Flock costs + $53,978-$67,824 per RTCC technician, against a documented county budget deficit, a February 2026 hiring freeze and expiring ARPA funds. Pair it with the security-liability argument (Condor exposure, search-reason leak, Douglas County camera hack) rather than a privacy-first frame.

STRUCTURAL: chieftain.com, coloradonewsline.com, dcj.colorado.gov, post.colorado.gov, theguardian.com and 9news.com block automated fetching, and both the CivicClerk council portal (puebloco.portal.civicclerk.com) and the OpenGov budget are JavaScript-rendered. A periodic MANUAL BROWSER SESSION is now a structural requirement of this research. Top documentary gaps: the 2026-01-26 council agenda packet and video, and the Pueblo PD section of the 2026 budget.
